title: Garbage collection modes in microservices (server, workstation, containers)
hook: ASP.NET Core defaults to server garbage collection for throughput. Containerized APIs need heap hard limits so the process respects cgroup memory. Dynamic Adaptation To Application Sizes (DATAS) shrinks heaps when load is light.

blocks.text: Workstation garbage collection uses one heap and favors lower latency for desktop apps. Server garbage collection creates one heap per logical processor for higher throughput in services. In containers, set GCHeapHardLimit or GCHeapHardLimitPercent so the runtime does not assume all host RAM is available. DATAS (Dynamic Adaptation To Application Sizes) adjusts heap size based on actual memory pressure in modern .NET.

entries.plainDefinition: Multi-heap GC mode tuned for throughput on multi-core servers.
entries.example: Default for ASP.NET Core on Windows and Linux.

entries.plainDefinition: Single-heap GC mode favoring interactive app responsiveness.
Runtime feature that shrinks or grows GC heaps based on application memory usage.
entries.example: Light-traffic API uses less RAM until load increases.

blocks.text: A Kubernetes pod with a 512 MB limit and no GC heap cap can be OOM-killed while the runtime still thinks it has gigabytes. Calling GC.Collect() in request code rarely helps and often hurts. The knobs that matter: server versus workstation, heap hard limit, latency versus throughput mode, and fixing allocation traps — not manual collection.

blocks.title: Production defaults
blocks.body: Keep server GC for APIs. Set DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimitPercent or runtimeconfig GCHeapHardLimit in containers. Measure with dotnet-counters before changing GCServer or GCLatencyMode.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Confirm server GC
items.body: ASP.NET Core enables it by default; verify in runtimeconfig.

items.title: Set heap hard limit
items.body: Match cgroup memory limit minus native and stack overhead.

items.title: Enable DATAS if appropriate
items.body: Helps variable-load services use memory efficiently.

items.title: Monitor gen-2 and pause times
items.body: EventCounters or Application Insights; fix allocations before tweaking GC.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Calling GC.Collect() in request handlers. Running workstation GC on a 16-core API pod. Omitting heap limits in memory-constrained containers. Changing GC mode without measuring pause times and throughput.

interviewTakeaways: ASP.NET Core defaults to server GC for throughput.
Containers need heap hard limits aligned with cgroup memory.
Fix allocation rate before tweaking GC; never Collect in the hot path.
commonPitfalls: Switching to workstation GC on servers without a reason.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node uses --max-old-space-size. .NET uses GCHeapHardLimitPercent and respects cgroups in modern runtimes.
